title: Translating genomic data into healthcare practice with the Singapore National Precision Medicine program.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC metadata: not open access, no full text, no supplement, no text-mined accessions; the NCBI PMC link (PMC13605287) is an unrelated MDPI Children review, not this paper. Fetched the PRECISE data-access page (updated 5 Aug 2026): the integrated dataset is accessible only through the TRUST platform with TRUST Data Access Committee approval. Fetched the c-BIG/sg10k-health GitHub README: Phase I SG10K_Health sites-only VCFs, multi-sample VCFs and Hail tables are 'on request to the NPM Data Access Committee'. Zenodo DOI search returned 0 records.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Abstract only: PRECISE-SG100K multi-ancestry Asian population dataset, familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) translation use case, phase III plans. Web search snippets (not opened as files) mention 102,202 genomes and a query-only CHORUS variant browser for SG10K_Health; no bulk open download of allele frequencies was found.

a1_downloadable.note: Controlled access: PRECISE-SG100K genomes and linked EHR (electronic health records) only via the TRUST platform plus TRUST Data Access Committee; SG10K_Health summary VCFs also gated by the NPM DAC (Data Access Committee). Checked the access pages; no open file found.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not checkable; the paper is a programme overview, and any label (e.g. FH diagnosis, LDL cholesterol) would sit in controlled phenotype/EHR tables.

a3_inputs_present.note: No inputs downloadable; genotypes are controlled access.

a5_enough_rows.note: About 100,000 participants per the access page, but no rows seen.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: unknown; whole-genome VCFs for ~100k people are terabyte-scale
a6_fits_laptop.note: Raw genotype data would not fit a laptop; only summary-level data might, and none is openly downloadable.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not assessable without access to the phenotype tables.

honest_claim_h3: No claim possible: no openly downloadable data accompanies this programme-overview paper.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use genetic variants and routine blood lipid tests from Singaporean adults to predict who carries an inherited high-cholesterol mutation.
plain_idea.train_on: Whole-genome variant calls plus clinical lab values for each participant in the Singapore cohort; number of usable examples unknown because the data is controlled access.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a person has genetically confirmed familial hypercholesterolemia (an inherited condition causing very high LDL cholesterol), from clinical genetic testing.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Most such screening models were built on European-ancestry cohorts; a Chinese/Malay/Indian cohort would test whether they transfer, but only with an approved access application.

ml_idea: Ancestry-transfer test of FH (familial hypercholesterolemia) screening models on Asian cohorts; blocked by controlled access through TRUST and the NPM Data Access Committee.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Confirm whether any open, bulk-downloadable allele-frequency table exists for SG10K_Health or SG100K; none found on the access pages or GitHub.

verdict_reason: A1 fails: controlled access (PRECISE TRUST platform plus TRUST Data Access Committee; SG10K_Health via NPM DAC). The paper is a programme overview with no open supplement, and no open summary-level download was found.
